title: Product investigation - 123 school
heading: Product investigation
intro: You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.question: What is the end point of a titration?

answers.b: the moment the indicator changes colour
answers.c: the moment the solution starts to boil
answers.d: the moment the burette is empty

questions.question: With which piece of glassware do you add liquid accurately in a titration?
1.0 mL of sodium hydroxide solution reacts with 3.0 mg of acetic acid. 12.0 mL of sodium hydroxide solution is needed. How many mg of acetic acid was in the sample?
The sample from the previous question contained 36 mg of acetic acid in 20 mL. What is the content in mg/mL?
What is the pH of a basic solution?
What colour is phenolphthalein in a basic solution?
An indicator is yellow below pH 6.0 and blue above pH 7.6. What colour is the indicator at pH 9?
Which BINAS table gives the colour change range of indicators?
What is breaking down with the help of light called?
What is breaking down with the help of electricity called?
Which substances are formed in the electrolysis of water?
How do you show the presence of oxygen?
How do you show the presence of hydrogen?

answers.c: with a burning splint you hear a pop

questions.question: How do you show the presence of carbon dioxide?
How do you show the presence of water?

answers.d: a burning splint goes out with a bang

questions.question: Which precipitate forms when sodium chloride solution and silver nitrate solution are mixed? (use BINAS table 35)
You dilute 10 mL of a solution with water to 100 mL. What is the dilution factor?
A solution of 50 g/L is diluted 10 times. What is the new concentration?
You take 25 mL of a solution of 40 g/L and add water to make 500 mL. What is the new concentration?
You see a yellow flame colour. Which metal ion was in the substance? (use BINAS table 38)
In which BINAS table do you look up an E number?
What is E-420 used for? (use BINAS table 45)
A label says: "Contains water, sugar, citric acid". Which substance is present in the largest amount?
In which BINAS table do you find the meaning of hazard symbols on a label?
Which separation method do you use to remove an insoluble solid from a liquid?
Which separation method do you use to separate two liquids with different boiling points?
Which separation method do you use to get dissolved salt out of a solution?
In which separation method does a substance stick to the surface of a solid (such as activated carbon)?
